assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1 based drugs is a rare case in which basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, insulinotropic action, intestinal and CNS effects) led directly to therapies that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst and Drucker made the decisive physiological and mechanistic discoveries on GLP-1 secretion, action and trophic effects; Knudsen led the translational design of the long-acting analogues that made the biology a medicine. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is real but the credit is contested, and Habener, a central figure, is not among the credited names, so the three-person split is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: decades of independent confirmation, large randomized outcome trials and global clinical use. Recognition is timely, arguably pressing given the scale of impact.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, Habener and industry scientists is disputed and the supplied credited list omits Habener.
Whether the committee wishes to honour an industry-led drug development component alongside physiology is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general method for causal control of genetically defined cells with millisecond precision, and has reshaped circuit analysis across the nervous system and beyond. It is an invention of lasting methodological importance rather than a single disease discovery.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and the demonstration of neuronal control (Boyden, Deisseroth, also Miesenbock's earlier genetic photostimulation) make this a six-person credit problem that cannot fit three laureates without leaving out figures whose contributions are widely regarded as decisive.
assessment.maturity: Mature: twenty years of widespread independent use, with early clinical translation (retinal optogenetic vision restoration) still emerging. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Credit is genuinely contested among Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann, Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenbock.
Clinical translation is nascent, so the prize case rests on methodology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells, particularly CD19 CAR-T, produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapeutics. The discovery is clear, original in design (chimeric receptors with costimulatory domains) and of strong clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June both developed the costimulated second-generation CAR concept and led the clinical proof; Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early CAR trials are important but arguably a related adjacent case. Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work is not in the credited names, which is an attribution gap.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough: multiple approved products and long-term remission data beyond ten years in some patients; open issues are toxicity, cost, limited efficacy in solid tumours and secondary malignancy surveillance.
uncertainties: Foundational chimeric receptor contribution by Eshhar is not among the credited names.
Long-term safety and solid-tumour efficacy remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic, ER-to-nucleus communication, with mechanistic clarity (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK) and relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell physiology. It is an elegant, original, textbook-level discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the two scientists most associated with discovering and mechanistically resolving the pathway, with complementary contributions in yeast and mammalian cells. Credit is comparatively clean, though others such as Ron contributed to related arms.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of confirmation across species with a stable mechanistic picture. Therapeutic translation is still limited, which does not weaken the basic-discovery case.
uncertainties: Contributions of David Ron, Jonathan Weissman and others to the broader PERK/integrated stress response arms are not in the credited list.
A two-person split could be criticised if a third laureate were wanted for the ER-signalling field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical, anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers, with population-level reductions in CIN and cervical cancer already documented. This is a large public-health achievement built on a clear discovery.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller made the decisive demonstration that L1 forms immunogenic VLPs; Frazer (with Jian Zhou, who is not credited and who died in 1999) contributed the early VLP expression. Zur Hausen's HPV-cancer link was already recognised in 2008, which sharpens the question of how much new discovery remains.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with registry evidence of effectiveness against cervical cancer across countries. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Jian Zhou's role cannot be represented in the credited names.
Overlap with the 2008 prize for HPV discovery may make the committee hesitant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term culture of adult stem cell derived epithelial organoids, built on the Lgr5 stem cell discovery, created a widely used model system for development, regeneration, host-microbe interaction, cancer and personalised therapy testing. Impact is very broad.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 identification and the organoid concept, with Sato as the principal experimental lead of the first intestinal organoid paper. Credit is fairly clear for these two, though pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work is a separate lineage not covered here.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: broad independent adoption, but clinical benefit is still prospective and standardisation questions remain.
uncertainties: Translational and diagnostic benefit is not yet demonstrated at scale.
Relationship to other organoid lineages (pluripotent stem cell derived) might fragment recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib proved that rationally targeted inhibition of an oncogenic kinase (BCR-ABL) can convert a fatal leukaemia into a manageable chronic condition, establishing the paradigm for precision oncology. Impact is historic and the discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are the principal credited figures. Rowley and Witte, who established the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL oncogenicity, are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with long-term survival data, though the novelty has been partly overtaken by many later targeted therapies, which can reduce the sense of timeliness.
uncertainties: The foundational cytogenetic and oncogene work is outside the credited names.
The committee may judge the drug-development component to be closer to pharmacology than discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery that BCL-2 blocks cell death rather than promoting proliferation redefined cancer biology, linked oncogenes to apoptosis and led to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax for CLL and AML. It is a well-defined conceptual and translational contribution, though apoptosis was already recognised in 2002 through C. elegans work.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterised BCL-2 and the Bcl-2 family biology, and Vaux demonstrated the survival-promoting function in 1988; Strasser extended the family and pathway work. Tsujimoto's cloning of BCL2 from the t(14;18) is not in the credited names, a notable gap.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with approved targeted therapies and extensive independent confirmation of the mechanism. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer, who made parallel BCL2 discoveries, are not credited.
Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize may reduce perceived novelty.
